On 2023/05/23 (Tue) 14:38 the user and I discussed how schools and universities can use virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR) for immersive learning during COVID-19 travel restrictions. #vr-ar-education #conversation-2023-05-23

VR/AR education use cases we discussed: virtual field trips, surgical/lab simulations for medical students, AR language learning, VR historical reenactments, collaborative learning in a shared virtual space, and all-in-one cross-country inclusive classrooms. #vr-ar-education

VR/AR education resources I recommended: edtech vendors zSpace, Google Expeditions and Nearpod; conferences/events VRX (Virtual Reality Learning Experience), AR in Education Conference, EdTechXEurope; online communities Reddit, VR/AR Association, EdTechXGlobal; training programs Veative VR Teacher Training, Adobe Immersive Learning, Google AR/VR Teacher Training. #vr-ar-education

Barriers to scaling VR/AR in schools I listed: cost of hardware/software/infrastructure, lack of technical expertise and interoperability issues, insufficient teacher training, ethical and data-privacy concerns, and accessibility for students with disabilities. #vr-ar-education

VR/AR education resources I recommended: edtech vendors zSpace, Google Expeditions, Nearpod; training programs Veative VR Teacher Training, Adobe Immersive Learning, Google AR/VR Teacher Training. #vr-ar-education

Privacy/ethics points for VR/AR in education I gave: data privacy and security of the large amounts of personal data collected, inclusivity/non-discrimination, intentional and appropriate use to protect student mental health, and obtaining parental/student consent plus informing them of data collection. #vr-ar-education

Regulations and standards I cited for VR/AR privacy in education: GDPR (EU, explicit consent), FERPA (US student records), COPPA (US, children under 13), ISO/IEC 27001 (information security management); plus ethics guidance from XR Association, EdTech UK and ISTE. #vr-ar-education

My stance in that VR/AR education discussion: the tech will enhance rather than replace traditional teaching, since in-person teacher/peer connection can't be replicated; it can personalize learning, improve accessibility for students with disabilities, rural or disadvantaged backgrounds, and enable lifelong learning. #vr-ar-education #user

User builds ODE models of gene regulation: activator protein A, production rate constant k1, degradation rate constant k2, substrate/inhibitor concentration, Hill coefficient n, dissociation constant Kd. #gene-regulation #ode-model #hill-equation

Replacing k1 with Hill kinetics for an activator gives d[A]/dt = kmax*[S]^n/(Kd^n + [S]^n) - k2*[A], where the Hill term is the production rate and k2*[A] the degradation rate. #activator-protein #hill-equation

User proposed d[A]/dt = k2 + kmax*[S]^n/(Kd^n + [S]^n) - k2*[A] and I told them it is wrong: the extra leading k2 basal term doesn't represent production or degradation; correct form drops it. #activator-protein #hill-equation

For a repressor R with inhibitor I: d[R]/dt = kmax*[I]^n/(Kd^n + [I]^n) - k2*[R], the same Hill form as the activator but driven by inhibitor concentration and producing repression. #repressor-protein #hill-equation
